title: llm-usage-metrics machine export line (v1)
description: One NDJSON line of `llm-usage machine export`. A bundle is a header line, zero or more file lines, then an end line; a bundle without its end line is incomplete.

version.description: Bundle format version; readers reject versions they do not know.

cliVersion.description: llm-usage-metrics version that wrote the bundle.

hostname.description: Host name of the exporting machine.

parserVersions.description: Source id to the parser version the export read it with. Optional: older exports leave it out, and readers that predate it ignore it.

gitRemotes.description: Each git root on the exporting machine (a repository or a worktree) whose repository has an origin, to that remote as host/path, lower-cased, without scheme, credentials, port or .git. Optional: older exports leave it out, and readers that predate it ignore it.

singleRequestFlag.description: Events carry singleRequest. Optional: older exports leave it out, and readers take the flag from the event's source (antigravity, claude, gemini, opencode, pi).

file.description: The events of one counted file the reader does not hold at this revision.

filePath.description: Path of the file on the exporting machine.

revision.description: Opaque; changes exactly when the file's events, tool calls or messages change.

events.description: Unpriced usage events: costUsd is present only when the source recorded it (costMode explicit).

sessionEvents.description: The file's tool calls and messages, in the order the source logged them. Optional: left out when the file has none and by older exports; readers that predate it ignore it. Never holds message text or tool input and output.

end.description: Every counted file, including those the reader already holds; a file it holds that is not listed is no longer counted.

eventCount.description: Total usage events across all listed files; tool calls and messages are not counted.

toolCall.description: A tool call: its name, how it ended and when, without its input or output.

messageId.description: The assistant message that made the call.

message.description: A user, assistant or system turn: its role, ids, model and text length, never its text.
